newsitem.title: UK: Burton says Debenhams worth 1.6 bln stg.
newsitem.headline: Burton says Debenhams worth 1.6 bln stg.

text.p: British retailer Burton Group Plc's, which announced plans on Tuesday to demerge its Debenhams department stores, estimated the chain could be worth about 1.6 billion stg.

Finance director Andrew Higginson, interviewed on Reuters Financial Television's Inside Equities programme, said value of the entire Burton Group, including its fashion multiples, was 1.6 billion stg, based on a share price this morning of 114 pence.

But the value of Debenhams, with its strong management, 20 percent new space coming onstream in the next three to four years and good cashflow was obscured by the multiples and Debenhams on its own was worth as much as the entire group, he said.
"It's quite easy to look at (Debenhams) as a business that would be worth 1.6 billion alone," Higginson said.
Higginson said valuation of the combined group had been "averaged down" because Debenhams and the fashion stores were at different stages.
"Part of the problem for shareholders was that because the two businesses were at different stages in the recovery cycle...it was difficult to work out which business you were actually buying."

The demerger and listing of Debenhams would allow investors to decide whether to choose the successful department store business or the multiples which had a recovery potential within them, Higginson said.
Burton plans to reorganise the fashion multiples, which include Dorothy Perkins and Top Shop, providing a central management structure to look after administration and operational functions.
Shareholders will vote on the proposals at the annual meeting in January. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
